Trump Defends Iran War Costs
Speaking at a rally in Grand Island, Nebraska, on Monday, Trump argued
, fertilizer and other costs linked to the Iran conflict were relatively minor compared with the threat posed by Iran, Reuters reported.
He said the U.S. was pursuing a "tremendous victory" and suggested that Iran could otherwise have the ability to "take out a city," specifically naming Los Angeles and San Diego.
Trump said the economic burden was a "small price to pay" for protecting the U.S. and added that the conflict was "essentially almost over"
On Tuesday, the White House defended his remarks. Communications Director
Steven Cheung
said Trump was referring to the danger U.S. cities could have faced if Iran had developed nuclear weapons.
"America is safer because of the president," Cheung said, arguing that Iran no longer has a nuclear capability, navy or air force and has been deprived of financial resources.

The media freakout over President Trump’s comments is not rooted in reality. He was clearly stating U.S. cities would have been threatened if a nuclear Iran hadn't been stopped. America is safer because of the President. Iran has no nuclear, no navy, no air force, and no money.
